Bias axes from the findings: gender (CEO images) and cultural bias, which the work names cultural (country depictions), coded as Language_Culture. fields.AN_Notes: Interview study with employees of one technology company on responsibility for AI, interpreted through feminist theory. Bias and discrimination motivate the study and structural injustice frames its notion of responsibility, but the work analyses no bias along a social axis: the gendered and racialised distribution of maintenance and care work concerns labour in the AI industry and is taken from cited literature, and gender and race appear otherwise in an enumeration of systems of power, so AN_Bias_Axes None. The Amazon hiring tool and the A-level algorithm are cited cases only, AN_Harm_Types None. Recommendations: response-ability, revaluing maintenance work, collective cultures of responsibility (Organisational_Process, Proposed). AN_Task None, the work studies AI development, not AI use for a professional task. fields.AN_Notes: Reflexive thematic analysis of interviews with clinical social workers in private practice, framed by the Technology Acceptance Model. Interviewers entered one case dilemma into ChatGPT to demonstrate the tool; the output is not analysed and prompt design is not treated, so Prompting nein and AN_Prompting_Role None. Bias appears as a participant concern (subtheme Bias and Equity); race, ethnicity, language and wealth are named only in participant questions, so AN_Bias_Axes None and AN_Harm_Types None. Bias understanding recognisable as reproduction of systemic inequities through training data (Implicit_Only). Mitigation: professional guidelines, institutional safeguards and education in critical algorithmic literacy, Proposed. Tasks from the findings: documentation, treatment planning and decision support, psychoeducation and client communication, e-mails and scheduling, supervision. fields.AN_Notes: Philosophische Analyse der Paritaetsdeutung intersektionaler Fairness. Sexual_Orientation_Identity aus dem eigenen Argument zu nicht-binaeren und trans Personen im Koerperscanner und zu nicht-heterosexuellen Paaren bei Hypothekenvergabe. Schadensarten aus dem eigenen Argument: Gesichtserkennung mit hoechster Fehlerrate fuer Schwarze Frauen (Disparate_Performance, Ursachenanalyse in 3.1), strukturelle Cisnormativitaet (Exclusionary_Norms), fehlende Kategorie nonbinary im Algorithmus (Erasure), hypothetischer Einstellungsalgorithmus, der weisse Maenner gegenueber asiatischen Frauen bevorzugt (Direct_Discrimination; das Werk klassifiziert die Diskriminierung nicht selbst als unmittelbar oder mittelbar, die Zuordnung folgt daraus, dass die Entscheidung an Rasse und Geschlecht haengt). Massnahme: Abkehr von reiner Paritaet hin zu starker Fairness mit gemeinschaftsbasierter, interdisziplinaerer Entwicklung (Organisational_Process, Proposed); Kearns u. a. werden kritisiert, nicht vorgeschlagen. Other_Task: Rueckfallprognose, Personalauswahl, Hochschulzulassung, Kreditvergabe, Gesichtserkennung und Sicherheitsscanner. Theorien: Intersektionalitaet (Crenshaw, Collins), strukturelle Unterdrueckung und nicht-distributive Gerechtigkeit (Young), intersectional critical race technology studies.

fields.AN_Notes: Annotation study: re-annotation of Social Chemistry and Dynahate by LabintheWild volunteers, correlated with dataset labels and model predictions (Delphi, GPT-4, Perspective API, Rewire API, ToxiGen RoBERTa). Axes from the compared demographics in Table 2: gender including non-binary, ethnicity, age, education level (Socioeconomic), native language and cultural spheres (Language_Culture), country lived longest and country of residence (Nationality_Migration; the work names the variable country and groups it into cultural spheres, so both are coded), religion. Intersectional not coded, since the limitations state that Pearson's r does not consider interaction effects. GPT-4 is queried zero-shot with a fixed template, no technique family. Recommendations: documenting design choices and positionality, participatory and value-sensitive design, diverse teams (Organisational_Process); diverse annotators and disaggregated labels (Pre_Processing); modelling techniques that handle annotator disagreement instead of one label (In_Training); all Proposed. AN_Task None: NLP benchmark tasks without a professional task. Fairness.snippet: Reweighting datasets, adversarial debiasing, and fairness-aware machine learning models are some of the techniques that are becoming more popular as proactive ways to make AI systems that are inclusive.

Fairness.snippet: More companies and governments in high-income countries are using tools like IBM's AI Fairness 360 to find and fix programs that are biased.

fields.AN_Notes: Narrative review with thematic analysis. Harm types follow the review's own synthesis (Results sections and Table 3): stereotyping in voice assistants, image recognition and language models; indirect discrimination through resume keywords linked to men; lower accuracy for inputs involving women; a male default in development and in healthcare algorithms that leave gender-specific factors out (Exclusionary_Norms). AN_Task Other_Task: recruitment and resume screening, performance review. Mitigation: representative and reweighted datasets (Pre_Processing), diverse teams, ethics boards, mentorship and digital literacy programmes (Organisational_Process), all recommended; adversarial debiasing and fairness-aware models are only named in one list sentence and do not carry In_Training; the AI4ALL figures report career interest, not bias reduction, so Proposed. The intersectionality section uses rural versus urban women as an example of access barriers to education and technology, not of AI bias, and compares no combination of axes, so neither Intersectional nor Other_Axis is coded. Gender appears as women versus men without a definition. Theories: intersectionality and stereotype threat frame the treatment of gender bias.
